title: Commission and lock a compact industrial robot-axis shock absorber
objective: With the representative axis isolated, physically seat a hex bit and loosen—but do not extract—the captive setscrew in the moving numbered collar; withdraw the bit, rotate the collar within its published 180° adjustment, reacquire the relocated socket, relock the setting, physically operate a guarded cycle control, and iteratively obtain two repeatable carriage stops without bottoming, overload, excessive rebound, or setting drift.
skills: hex-bit withdrawal and socket reacquisition after collar motion
controlled fine rotation of a small numbered collar
bimanual counterholding without invented torsional spring load
iterative adjustment from observed dynamic response
success_conditions: Use a rigid PhysX carriage with physically simulated drive, contact, axial return spring, 12.0 mm damper stroke, and external hard stop. Test energy must be at least 0.85 J—5% of the published 17.0 Nm/cycle maximum—and impact velocity must remain within 0.3–3.30 m/s and the conservative usable-setting bound read from the ECO OEM Small Series chart. The robot must loosen the captive setscrew, withdraw the bit, turn the collar, reacquire the moved socket, relock it, and physically initiate each test. Success requires two consecutive measured stops without exceeding stroke, striking the hard stop, exceeding published reaction/propelling limits, excessive rebound, or post-lock collar drift. Partial credit covers safe engagement, unlocking, adjustment, reacquisition, and locking. Zero score applies to energized adjustment, dropped tools, thread damage, unsafe collision, hard-stop impact, direct task-object pose/velocity/damping writes, collision suppression, welding, teleportation, or hidden demo-stage success flags.
industrial_value: The AZ-100 robot manual identifies shock-absorber adjustment as robot-axis maintenance. The Enidine catalog independently documents a compact adjustable hydraulic shock absorber, its geometry, operating limits, adjustment collar, and setscrew locking. The representative fixture therefore models an industrial commissioning operation without claiming that the Enidine unit is interchangeable with the AZ-100 component or that an unpublished manufacturer force curve is reproduced.
dexterity: The task combines small-socket tool alignment, controlled torque, counterholding, collar regrasping, mandatory tool withdrawal and reacquisition after the socket moves, retention of a fine setting during relocking, and feedback-driven dynamic commissioning. Its outcome depends on measured stopping behavior rather than knob rotation alone.

asset_plan: Author a full-scale representative non-button ECO OEM .35M-form fixture using 12.0 mm stroke, M16×1.5 housing thread, D=4.0 mm piston rod diameter, G=11.2 mm adjustment-knob diameter, H=14.5 mm axial knob length, F=87.4 mm indicated housing portion, and A=100.6 mm overall envelope. Do not mix optional-button A1/E1 dimensions into this version. Preserve the moving 180° collar and a captive contact-bearing setscrew. An independently authored M3×3 DIN 916-style screw with 0.5 mm pitch and 1.5 mm socket may be disclosed as a representative prototype choice, not an Enidine specification. Use a guarded rigid carriage near 1 J and 0.5 m/s, then validate at 240 Hz: energy balance, stroke, hard-stop contact, reaction and propelling loads, rebound, low/high-setting controls, lock retention, socket contact, parameter sensitivity, and clean reset. The robot must physically press the cycle control; no episode-time teleportation, welding, or direct state completion is allowed.
risk: The catalog does not publish collar torque, the original setscrew dimensions, friction, or a force-versus-setting calibration. These must remain disclosed bounded assumptions and pass component sensitivity, contact, stability, and witness-torque tests before YAM integration. The source chart must be conservatively digitized for the chosen velocity, and the representative damping law must not be described as manufacturer calibrated. The phase-15 reach result is only an IK planning lead, not grasp, collision, contact, or simulation validation.
